title: Ukrainian tennis star Dayana Yastremska says family home hit by Russian missile
content:
Ukrainian tennis player Dayana Yastremska says her family’s apartment in Odesa was hit by a Russian missile Friday evening.

The former world No. 21 and 2024 Australian Open semifinalist posted video and pictures on her Instagram account that show extensive damage to the apartment building, which she said had been directly struck by a missile.

Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and has repeatedly targeted Odesa, the strategically important Black Sea port city where Yastremska was born. She fled Ukraine with her younger sister Ivanna shortly after the war began, while their parents remained in the country.

“This is what the ‘Russian world’ looks like,” Yastremska wrote on Instagram.

The Ukrainian tagged the WTA and International Tennis Federation in the post and said the images showed the “true meaning of your ‘neutrality.’”

Russian and Belarusian players have been permitted to compete internationally without representing their countries since the invasion, while the Russian and Belarusian tennis federations remain suspended from ITF membership and international team competitions.

Russian attacks across Ukraine on Saturday killed at least six people and injured dozens, according to Ukrainian officials, with strikes reported in Odesa, Zaporizhzhia, Kryvyi Rih and the Zhytomyr region.

Odesa regional governor Oleh Kiper said 37 people, including an infant, were injured during the overnight attacks and two people were missing.

Russia’s defence ministry said its forces had targeted industrial facilities and cargo ships in Ukrainian ports. Russia has repeatedly denied deliberately targeting civilians.

The 26-year-old Yastremska is not the first Ukrainian tennis player to describe the war directly affecting her family.

In May, Marta Kostyuk said a missile destroyed a building around 100 metres from her parents’ home in Kyiv hours before she won her first-round match at the French Open.

Kostyuk later said she had “adapted to the fact that the tour forgot about it,” referring to the WTA.

The WTA said at the time that it unequivocally condemned Russia’s war on Ukraine and had consistently supported Ukrainian players since the invasion began.

Yastremska experienced a similar incident in January 2024, when she said a rocket had struck the Odesa building where her grandmother lived.
